newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds slip, spreads widen by a hair.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds slip, spreads widen by a hair.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities dipped into negative territory and spreads to Treasuries were unchanged to slightly wider in light trading Wednesday afternoon.

Most pass-throughs modestly underperformed their Treasury counterparts amid the Treasury's auction of $12.5 billion of five-year notes. But one head trader at a New York investment firm said the selloff was not auction related.
"There are sellers of mortgages versus Treasuries ... not auction related, but just in general," he said.
At this point, however, there are better buying opportunities in discount pass-throughs, the trader added.
In late trade, mortgages were 5/32 to 11/32 lower overall, while comparable Treasuries were off 5/32 to 9/32.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was off 8/32 at 100-22/32, yielding 119 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 9/32 at 100-24/32, and Freddie Mac paper was down 11/32 to 100-29/32.
Five-year Treasuries were off 5/32 at 6.77 percent, and 10-year notes were off 9/32 at 6.87 percent.
